name: Amazon
title: How Amazon makes money, live: revenue, AWS, ads and where it goes
description: Amazon's $716.9B year as a live clock: online stores, third-party sellers, ads, Prime and AWS, where the money goes, capex, and per employee. From the FY2025 10-K.
tagline: AWS is 18% of sales but 57% of operating income. Capex hit $131.8B.

10k: Amazon.com, Inc., Form 10-K for the year ended Dec 31, 2025 (filed Feb 6, 2026)
facts: SEC EDGAR XBRL companyfacts, Amazon.com, Inc. (CIK 0001018724): annual figures from each year's 10-K

blocks.label: projected from annual 10-K averages
blocks.note: Each counter = 2025 total from the 10-K ÷ 31,536,000 seconds. These are averages, not real-time sales. Capital spending = purchases of property and equipment in the cash flow statement ($131.8B, before $3.5B of proceeds and incentives). [[10k]]

sections.title: Money in, money out
sections.lede: Every dollar of 2025 revenue, from where it came to where it went. Values in US$ billions.

blocks.title: Income statement, 2025
blocks.note: US$ millions from the 10-K: 269,287 + 22,561 + 172,162 + 68,635 + 49,619 + 128,725 + 5,935 = 716,924 net sales. "G&A and other" = G&A 11,172 + other operating expense 4,639 (includes a $2.5B FTC settlement charge). Non-operating income, net of 17,336 = interest income 4,381 − interest expense 2,274 + other income 15,229, which the 10-K attributes mainly to equity-investment valuation adjustments, not cash from selling goods. "Income tax & equity-method" = 19,087 + 554. [[10k]]

blocks.title: Where the cash went, 2025

nodes.label: Capex, net of sale proceeds & incentives

blocks.note: Operating cash flow 139,514 − purchases of property and equipment 131,819 + proceeds from sales and incentives 3,499 = free cash flow 11,194, as the 10-K defines it (it was 38,219 in 2024). Amazon paid no dividends (none in the cash flow statement) and made no buybacks in 2023, 2024 or 2025; $6.1B remains on the 2022 authorization. [[10k]]

sections.title: Per employee
sections.lede: About 1,576,000 full-time and part-time employees at year-end, plus contractors and temporary staff that are not counted. [[10k]]

items: Net income ÷ employees; includes $15.2B of investment gains [[10k]]
The 10-K gives headcount only, no pay data [[10k]]

sections.title: Where the money comes from
sections.lede: Amazon reports three segments, revenue by product and service group, and revenue by country. It does not disclose revenue by US state.

blocks.title: Segments, 2025
blocks.note: Margins are derived. AWS earns 57% of operating income (45,606 ÷ 79,975, derived). [[10k]]

items.title: of operating income from 18% of sales
items.text: AWS sales grew 20% to $128.7B at a 35.4% operating margin (derived). North America earned 7.0% and International 2.9%. Retail and AWS are different businesses in one filing.

items.title: of capex, up from $83.0B
items.text: Purchases of property and equipment were $52.7B in 2023, $83.0B in 2024 and $131.8B in 2025. Of 2025's $142.4B total net additions, $96.5B went to AWS. Free cash flow fell from $38.2B to $11.2B.

items.title: of ad revenue, up 22%
items.text: Advertising sales grew from $46.9B in 2023 to $68.6B in 2025 (growth derived), now 9.6% of revenue (derived). The 10-K lists it as its own line.

items.title: in seller services revenue
items.text: Commissions plus fulfillment and shipping fees on sellers' products were 24% of revenue (derived), second only to Amazon's own online stores ($269.3B, 38% of revenue, derived).

items.title: of FTC settlement and severance in 2025
items.text: Operating income includes $2.5B for a settlement with the FTC and $2.7B of estimated severance costs, per the 10-K. Both are in the 2025 figures shown here.

items.title: in buybacks 2023–2025, and no dividends
items.text: Amazon keeps its cash for investment. There were no repurchases in 2023, 2024 or 2025, and the cash flow statement has no dividend line.

sections.title: Five years of results
sections.lede: Revenue, operating income and net income by year, from the 10-Ks.

items.text: Revenue $469.8B, operating income $24.9B, net income $33.4B. Capex $61.1B.
Revenue $514.0B, operating income $12.2B, a net loss of $2.7B, the only loss in the five years.
Revenue $574.8B, operating income $36.9B, net income $30.4B. Capex $52.7B.
Revenue $638.0B, operating income $68.6B, net income $59.2B. Capex $83.0B.
Revenue $716.9B (up 12%), operating income $80.0B, net income $77.7B. Capex $131.8B.
